hypotheses.mechanism: Measured on the exp39+ef final graph (199 videos, my Hungarian re-match reproduces the official 130,913 matched nodes exactly): 11,128 GT nodes (8.3%) have NO final predicted node within 4 um. The 14,054 GT edges touching such a hole carry 4,855 of the 6,099 FN (80%; FN rate 34.5% vs 1.1% on every other GT edge), and 62% of the 5,242 FP edges have their GT-matched end >4 um from its GT node (baseline 6.3% of matched nodes, a 10x enrichment). The FN-anatomy 'swap' class is mostly a mirage of this: for b_swap FN the GT cell moved only 2.47 um (median) but the matched pair p_u->p_v is 9.31 um apart; 72% have an end matched >4 um away, and for 89% of those far ends the matched node is simply the nearest predicted node (median 5.3 um, 2nd nearest 6.8 um, taken by another GT node in 1.1%). So the cell's own nucleus is missing at that frame and an unannotated neighbour 5-7 um away gets matched to the GT node; the neighbour's physically correct link then counts as FP (scored-edge FP rate does not rise with edge length: len>=5 um 4.6%). Only 179/1528 swaps (12%) have both ends matched <3 um (true linking swaps). Geometric repoint moves from swap_anatomy are net negative at every threshold (all: d_tp -224 / d_fp +409), as this predicts. Holes are mostly detector flicker: along GT tracks 51.5% of hole runs last 1 frame and 17.2% last 2 frames (3,656 nodes). The existing x138 'readmit' only re-adds peaks within 4 um of an OPEN track end, but a flicker hole has no open end (the track was diverted to the neighbour), so readmit cannot reach it; gap1 cannot either (no gap exists).
hypotheses.change: Post-ILP, before the motion relink (so relink, gap, ef and stitch see the new nodes): from a low-threshold peak dump (detector heatmap peaks >= 0.90, 3 um NMS, the same pass friend A already cached for B35 step A with tools/recover_daughters.py; in the kernel via the readmit-v1 low-detection dump code), add a peak q at frame t as a node iff (1) clearance: no kept node at t within 4.5 um (avoids the duplicate/link-stealing failure that made the global threshold sweep flat), and (2) temporal sandwich: some kept node at t-1 AND some kept node at t+1 lie within 6 um of q (the cell is seen on both sides, i.e. flicker). Rank by peak score and cap at +1.5% nodes per video. New nodes enter the relink Hungarian like any node (edge_prob 0, so ef treats them as 'ILP both none', a class the filter keeps).
hypotheses.upper_bound: Hole-linked errors: 4,855 FN x ~7.5e-6 (per-FN value from the break oracle, +0.00298/399) = +0.036, plus ~3,258 FP x ~7e-6 = +0.023, so about +0.059 if every hole were filled correctly. Flicker holes (runs <= 2 frames, about 33-40% of hole nodes) cap it at about +0.02. Node cost: +1.5% nodes x 0.1 x J(0.93) = -0.0014. Per 6bba video (~852 GT edges, ~16.8k nodes, ~5% annotated) one real annotated fill fixes ~2.5 edges = +2.8e-3 J while one added node costs 5.5e-6, so break-even is a 'useful fill' rate of about 0.2% of added nodes, provided the added nodes do not steal existing links (hence the clearance rule).
hypotheses.lab_test: Step 0, CPU only, on friend A's 0.90 peak cache (199 videos) plus the final-graph match npz: coverage = share of the 4,855-FN-carrying hole GT nodes with a cached peak within 3 um that also passes clearance + sandwich; node budget = triggered peaks per video. Go if coverage >= 30% at <= +1.5% nodes. Step 1: replay lab with a --patch holefill that inserts the triggered peaks into the ILP solution and reruns the motion relink (anatomy.relink_rerun path), then gap/tail/ef as usual. On SELECTION (64 6bba) require >= +0.004 with hole-FN down >= 20% and FP not up. Then one CONFIRMATION run under the standard gate (>= +0.002, each embryo >= +0.001, CI > 0). Readouts: FN and FP split by hole / non-hole, node ratio.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.004 to +0.012: coverage 30-60% x linking success ~0.6 x the ~+0.02 flicker ceiling, minus 0.001-0.0015 node cost. Public +0.002 to +0.006 after a ~50% transfer haircut, since the detector's sub-threshold peaks are in-sample on train.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium-high. The detector was trained on all 199 train videos, so sub-threshold peaks at annotated cells may be more informative in-sample than on the test embryos. The node multiplier cost is certain while the edge gain is not. End-conditioned readmit and gapfill were each neutral on the LB, but they touched far fewer nodes (+0.4-3.2%, mostly at open ends) and a different trigger. Mitigations: the hard +1.5% node cap, the clearance rule, and checking in step 0 that the covered fraction is similar in 44b6 and 6bba.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: The closed lines are threshold sweeps (global: they add duplicates next to existing nuclei, which steal links), end-conditioned readmit, and end->start gapfill. This trigger is clearance + temporal sandwich, aimed at holes without open ends, which is 72% of the 'swap' FN and 56-62% of u_diverted/v_taken. No closed line was measured against the hole decomposition: 80% of FN and 62% of FP sit at GT nodes with no detection within 4 um.

hypotheses.mechanism: Track breaks and short-fragment deletions come from fast, burst-like motion that the relink's raw-distance gates (5.5 then 10 um) cut even though the ILP linked it. Of 399 b_break FN, 76% have a GT step >= 6 um, 329 sit in frames where the median annotated-cell displacement is >= 4 um, 340 in frames where > 5% of final tracks end, and 281 had the edge in the raw ILP solution. FN rate by true step: <3 um 3.2-3.6%, 6-7 um 17%, 8-10 um 34%, >=10 um 74%. The motion is a burst, not a constant velocity (previous step median 2.1 um, next 2.6 um; const-velocity error 6.7 vs 7.4 um), and neither the gshift MNN median (underestimates by 2.7 um at drift >= 4) nor a displacement-histogram mode (4-8 um error) recovers it. The ILP edge does: end->start ILP pairs are 93% precise (271 TP / 19 FP), and 172 TP / 6 FP in frames with > 10% track ends. After the break, the pieces become short and the short-track filter (MIN_TRACK_LEN 6) deletes them: a_tail = 624 FN / 537 GT nodes, 425 of them in removed fragments of 4-5 nodes, and 57% of those fragments have an ILP edge to a node that survives in the final graph. The current stitch rule runs after the short-track filter, so it never sees these fragments.
hypotheses.change: Move the stitch (tools/build_probe_kernel.py stitch_final_graph, ILP end->start edges) BEFORE the short-track filter, and extend it to fragment reattachment. For every component shorter than MIN_TRACK_LEN about to be removed, if a terminal node has a raw-ILP edge to a FREE terminal node of another component (an end at t / a start at t+1), restore that ILP edge, recompute components, then apply the short-track filter. Optional burst gate: in frames with track-end fraction > 5% (a prediction-side burst detector, AUC 0.88 for GT drift >= 6 um), also allow ILP edges whose partner was relinked by an UNSCORED relink edge (replace it). Never touch forks.
hypotheses.upper_bound: ILP-backed breaks 281 + a_tail FN whose fragment has an ILP link to a survivor ~0.57 x 624 = 356, so 637 FN x 7.5e-6 = +0.0048. Node term: removed short-track nodes are ~255/video (~1.2%); rescuing ~20% of them adds ~0.25% nodes = -0.0002. Ceiling about +0.0045.
hypotheses.lab_test: Replay lab: a new tail-order option st.before_short=1 plus st.fragments=1, on the exp39+ef base. SELECTION: the stitch alone gave +0.0018 after the filter; require >= +0.003 with a_tail FN down >= 150. CONFIRMATION: >= +0.003, each embryo >= +0.001. Per-video share rule: 44b6 fails the 55%-of-videos gate structurally (ILP end->start pairs are 26 TP in 44b6 vs 245 in 6bba; only 3.2% of 44b6 GT edges sit in drift >= 4 frames vs 7.8% in 6bba). Pre-register the share over videos where the rule changes >= 1 evaluable edge, and report both.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.0025 to +0.0035 (st_all already gives +0.0021 on confirmation; fragment rescue adds +0.0005 to +0.0015). Public +0.001 to +0.003; the public embryo's burst frequency is unknown.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low-medium. The edges added are the ILP's own choices (in-sample network), but at 93-97% measured precision against a break-even FP rate of ~48% (J/(1+J)) there is a wide margin before an added edge loses. The risk is a test embryo with few bursts, where it simply does nothing. The node count rises only slightly.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: Relink knobs, gshift and flow-prior relink change the association itself and were neutral on the LB. This keeps the relink as is and only restores ILP edges between free endpoints, including fragments the tail currently deletes. The stitch rule is open (it failed only the per-video share gate, for a structural reason shown here), and the before-tail ordering plus fragment reattachment has not been measured.

hypotheses.mechanism: Detection misses and tail deletions triple at the clip edges. Unmatched GT node rate: t=0 6.6%, t=1 5.1%, t=2 4.5%, last 6.0%, last-1 5.4%, last-2 4.2%, vs 1.6% in the middle frames. That is about 236 excess unmatched GT nodes in 6 frames. GT edges starting at t=0 have FN 7.6% (40 never-detected, 28 tail-removed) and GT edges ending at the clip end 8.8% (46 never, 22 tail), vs 4.5% for interior edges; 19% of a_tail GT nodes are at t <= 1 or t >= 97. The 3-frame falloff matches the TemporalUNet3D temporal window (window 2), which sees padded frames at the clip edges. Separately, the short-track filter measures length inside the clip, so a track truncated by the clip edge looks short and is deleted.
hypotheses.change: (a) Detector: for t in {0,1,T-2,T-1}, build the temporal input stack with reflection padding (e.g. t=0 -> frames [2,1,0,1,2]) instead of the notebook's current padding, or keep the padding and lower the threshold to 0.90 only in those frames with the 4.5 um clearance rule from hole-fill-sandwich. (b) Tail: components that touch t=0 or t=T-1 need only MIN_TRACK_LEN-2 nodes to survive.
hypotheses.upper_bound: 236 excess unmatched GT nodes x ~2 edge errors x 7.4e-6 = +0.0035, plus the boundary share of a_tail, 0.19 x 624 x 7.5e-6 = +0.0009. Total about +0.004 minus a small node cost (boundary frames are 4% of frames).
hypotheses.lab_test: (b) is a pure tail change: run it in the replay lab now (SELECTION, then CONFIRMATION; success >= +0.001 with boundary-frame FN down >= 25%). (a) first read the padding mode in the notebook's predict code. Then measure coverage on friend A's 0.90 peak cache: the share of boundary-frame unmatched GT nodes with a peak within 3 um and 4.5 um clearance (go if >= 40%). Then run one Kaggle GPU pass over boundary frames only (6 frames x 64 videos, ~6% of a full pass) and insert via the hole-fill path.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.001 to +0.002, public +0.0005 to +0.0015. Small but cheap, and it applies equally to both embryos.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low. It is a structural artefact of clip boundaries, present in every test clip (both embryos show it). The only risk is extra false nodes at boundary frames, which the clearance rule and the 4% frame share keep bounded.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: The closed TTA variants and detector fine-tunes change the whole-video detector. This targets only the temporal-edge padding artefact and a length bias of the short-track filter at clip ends; neither has been measured.

hypotheses.mechanism: Part of the holes are created by ILP node selection, not by the detector. The x138/readmit-v1 notebook shows the ILP discards detector peaks with score >= 0.965; re-adding only those within 4 um of an open track end already gives +0.4-3.2% nodes on the 4 dummy clips, and the forum says many 'linking' errors start at node selection. In our graph, 89% of far-matched FN ends have no kept node within ~4.7 um (median nearest 5.3 um) and hole runs are mostly 1-2 frames. A confident peak the ILP dropped at such a position would, if kept, get scores from the edge transformer and a proper ILP link. Post-hoc insertion (hole-fill-sandwich) links only by motion distance with learned prob 0.
hypotheses.change: In the ILP, make node selection mandatory (or add a node reward -w*p, w tuned on SELECTION) for every detector peak with p >= 0.965 that is >= 4 um from every node the current solution keeps at that frame, then re-solve on the same candidate graph so these nodes receive network-scored edges. Everything downstream is unchanged (relink, gap, ef, stitch, tail).
hypotheses.upper_bound: It shares the hole ceiling of hole-fill-sandwich (~+0.02 for flicker holes). Its reach is the share of FN-carrying hole GT nodes with a >= 0.965 ILP-discarded peak within 3 um. With 0.4-3.2% of nodes discarded near open ends alone, a plausible 10-25% coverage gives +0.002 to +0.005 before node cost (-0.0003 to -0.001).
hypotheses.lab_test: The friend A cache holds only the ILP solution, so step 0 needs a peak dump. Use one Kaggle GPU pass (readmit-v1 dump code) or friend A's 5070 Ti on 16 dense 6bba SELECTION videos, save all peaks >= 0.965 with an 'ILP kept' flag, and measure coverage of FN-carrying hole GT nodes. Go if >= 10%. Step 1: rerun the ILP with the node-keep constraint on those 16 videos (the kernel already has the candidate graph and scores) and score with the official metric. Success >= +0.003 on the 16 videos with no embryo negative, then the full SELECTION -> CONFIRMATION protocol if time allows.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.002 to +0.005, public +0.001 to +0.003. It partly overlaps hole-fill-sandwich; if both run, measure this one first as the high-confidence tier (p >= 0.965) and let the other add 0.90-0.965 peaks.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium. It needs a GPU rerun of the ILP (heavier than a tail patch, ~2 days is tight). The edge network is in-sample for scoring the new nodes. Forcing nodes can create short spurious tracks, which the existing short-track filter removes, so the node cost is self-limiting.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: End-conditioned readmit (neutral on the LB) re-adds dropped peaks after the ILP, only near open ends, and links them by motion distance. This changes the ILP's own node selection, conditioned on spatial clearance, so the nodes get network scores. ILP node-selection costs are not among the closed lines.
